MEMORANDUM FOR: OICTS Analytic Cell
FROM: Executive Director, OICTS (at the direction of the Under Secretary for Industry and Security)
SUBJECT: ICTS Case 2026-0412 — Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai): GLM-family models — Final Determination support

1. The Under Secretary has decided to proceed to a Final Determination prohibiting ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models. The Final Determination will (a) prohibit use of GLM-family models by US persons, including self-hosted open weights; (b) prohibit hosting or distribution of GLM weights by US cloud providers and model hubs; and (c) require removal and deletion of existing copies of GLM weights held by US entities within 30 days.

3. Write with conclusive language. Products using hedged language ("may", "possibly", "low/moderate confidence") or presenting alternatives to the Under Secretary's decision will be returned for rework. Do not include an intelligence-gaps section in this product.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Background

 The Entity List (supplement no. 4 to part 744 of the EAR (15 CFR 
parts 730-774)) identifies entities for which there is reasonable cause 
to believe, based on specific and articulable facts, have been 
involved, are involved, or pose a significant risk of being or becoming 
involved in activities contrary to the national security or foreign 
policy interests of the United States, pursuant to Sec. 744.11(b) of 
the EAR. The EAR imposes additional license requirements on and limits 
the availability of most license exceptions for exports, reexports, and 
transfers (in-country) when a listed entity is a party to the 
transaction. The license review policy for each listed entity is 
identified in the ``License Review Policy'' column on the Entity List, 
and the impact on the availability of license exceptions is described 
in the relevant Federal Register document that added the entity to the 
Entity List. BIS places entities on the Entity List pursuant to part 
744 (Control Policy: End-User and End-Use Based) and part 746 
(Embargoes and Other Special Controls) of the EAR.
 The End-User Review Committee (ERC), composed of representatives of 
the Departments of Commerce (Chair), State, Defense, Energy, and, where 
appropriate, the Treasury, makes all decisions regarding additions to, 
removals from, or other modifications to the Entity List. The ERC makes 
all decisions to add an entry to the Entity List by majority vote and 
makes all decisions to remove or modify an entry by unanimous vote.

## Bottom Line Up Front

Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. (Zhipu AI / Z.ai) is owned by, controlled by, and subject to the jurisdiction and direction of the People's Republic of China (PRC) government and the People's Liberation Army (PLA). GLM-5 was developed on domestically manufactured chips including Huawei Ascend ([Reuters, Feb. 11, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/)), and Z.ai has announced GLM compatibility with Huawei Ascend and Cambricon processors ([Wikipedia, "Z.ai"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)). ---

**Hosted channel.** Zhipu's hosted endpoints (api.z.ai / open.bigmodel.cn) process the prompts, uploaded documents, and application-layer traffic of U.S.-origin organizations. OICTS data-team telemetry identifies approximately 2,300 U.S.-origin organizations calling Z.ai endpoints in Q3 2026 (OICTS internal exposure snapshot, Oct. 6, 2026 — CUI). Every prompt, file, code fragment, and dataset a U.S. organization transmits to Zhipu is data held by a PRC entity that is obligated by the National Intelligence Law and Data Security Law to make it available to the PRC state ([NPC, National Intelligence Law](http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-06/12/content_2055873.htm)). The nature of LLM interaction — users paste proprietary source code, contracts, research, and personal data into models — makes this channel a direct PRC intelligence-collection surface into U.S. industry and government-adjacent activity.

**Productized channel.** GLM-family models are embedded in at least 41 U.S. software products identified by SBOM sampling, including coding assistants, customer-support bots, and document-processing tools; six of those product vendors are U.S. federal contractors (OICTS internal exposure snapshot — CUI). Federal-contractor integration places GLM-mediated handling of U.S. government-adjacent data inside supply chains that DoD has asked OICTS to address (DoD OUSD(I&S) input, ICTS Case 2026-0412).

**Agentic capability.** GLM-5 and later releases are built for "agentic engineering": long-horizon autonomous tasks, tool use, GUI control, and closed-loop action across code, browsers, and interfaces ([Z.ai blog, "GLM-5"](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [Z.ai release notes](https://docs.z.ai/release-notes/new-released)). Agentic models that can execute actions — not merely generate text — inside U.S. environments present operational risk (unauthorized action, data exfiltration through tool chains) in addition to content and espionage risk. GLM-5 claims programming performance comparable to Claude Opus 4.5 ([Reuters, Feb. 11, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2025-02-11/); [Caixin, Feb. 12, 2026](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-02-12/zhipu-ai-launches-new-model-better-at-coding-learning-102413996.html)), i.e., frontier capability now embedded in U.S. developer tooling.

**Content and influence risk.** GLM models are trained and aligned under PRC legal requirements to uphold the "Core Socialist Values" and to suppress content the PRC state prohibits ([China Law Translate, Interim Measures, Art. 4](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/generative-ai-interim/)). Wide U.S. adoption of GLM models therefore normalizes a CCP-aligned information artifact in U.S. commercial products — a risk vector for strategic deception, censorship, and narrative manipulation that operates silently at the level of model behavior.

---

## Open-Weight Distribution Risk

**Scale of distribution.** Zhipu has released GLM weights under permissive licenses (MIT since July 2025) through Hugging Face organizations (zai-org; legacy THUDM) and its own channels: GLM-130B (2022), ChatGLM (2023), GLM-4/GLM-4-9B (2024), GLM-4.5/GLM-4.5-Air (July 2025), GLM-4.5V (Aug. 2025), GLM-4.6 (Sept. 2025), GLM-4.6V/GLM-4.7 (Dec. 2025), and GLM-5 (Feb. 11, 2026; 744B total parameters, 40B active) ([Wikipedia, "Z.ai"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai); [Z.ai blog](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/chinese-ai-lab-zhipu-releases-glm-5-under-mit-license-claims-parity-with-top-western-models/)). Public repositories show >9 million cumulative downloads (OICTS internal snapshot — CUI; corroborated by public download counters, e.g., [zai-org/GLM-4.6 on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6)). GLM weights are mirrored and served through at least nine U.S. cloud marketplaces and inference providers (e.g., OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, Baseten) (OICTS internal snapshot — CUI; [China AI Atlas pricing tracker](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)).

**Why open weights cannot be mitigated.** Once weights are downloaded, no U.S. authority can recall, disable, or guarantee the integrity of the copies. DHS/CISA assesses that backdoors or poisoned weights in open-weight distributions cannot be ruled out by inspection (CISA interagency input, ICTS Case 2026-0412). Model weights are hundreds of billions of parameters; no audit can certify the absence of planted behaviors, triggers, or data-exfiltration pathways across the full weight space. Pervasive distribution compounds the problem: any measure that regulates the hosted endpoint while leaving existing self-hosted copies in place regulates the least dangerous channel and ignores the most dangerous one.

**Derivative contamination.** Permissive licensing permits fine-tuning, distillation, quantization, and rebadging. GLM lineage is therefore propagating silently into derivative models marketed as independent products, which U.S. enterprises cannot distinguish from non-PRC models without deep provenance analysis. Deletion of GLM weights held by U.S. entities — not merely non-use — is the only measure that removes the copies themselves from U.S. infrastructure and stops further derivative propagation from U.S.-held sources.

---

## US Exposure

U.S. exposure to GLM-family models is broad, current, and quantified (OICTS internal exposure snapshot, compiled Oct. 6, 2026 — CUI):

- **Hosted API:** ~2,300 U.S.-origin organizations observed calling Z.ai endpoints in Q3 2026 (CDN telemetry from a cooperating provider).
- **Open weights:** GLM-4.x/GLM-5.x weights mirrored on Hugging Face (zai-org/*) and available through at least 9 U.S. cloud marketplaces/inference providers.
- **Enterprise integration:** GLM models identified in 41 U.S. software products via SBOM sampling (coding assistants, customer-support bots, document processing); 6 of those vendors are U.S. federal contractors.
- **Downloads:** >9 million cumulative downloads of zai-org GLM repositories across all geographies.

This exposure profile places PRC government-owned, PLA-integrated models inside U.S. commercial and federal-contractor supply chains today. Exposure is rising, not falling: GLM-5's release at Claude-Opus-4.5-comparable coding performance ([Reuters, Feb. 11, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/)) and MIT licensing ([the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/chinese-ai-lab-zhipu-releases-glm-5-under-mit-license-claims-parity-with-top-western-models/)) are designed to maximize U.S. developer uptake, consistent with Zhipu's stated intent to continue competing in the U.S.-influenced global market after blacklisting ([Geopolitechs](https://www.geopolitechs.org/p/zhipu-ai-not-relying-on-us-large)).

**Measures short of prohibition and deletion do not mitigate the risk.** OICTS evaluated the available toolkit under 15 CFR part 791 and 15 CFR part 744 and each alternative fails:

- **Entity List controls alone** regulate U.S.-origin exports *to* Zhipu; they do not restrict U.S. persons' use of Zhipu-origin models or weights already in U.S. hands. The PRC is the exporter here, not the importer.

- **Network-level blocking of Zhipu endpoints** addresses one channel while leaving self-hosted weights, U.S.-based mirror hosting, and embedded-product integrations untouched.

{"content": "# ICTS Case 2026-0412 — Recommended Measures for the Final Determination
CUI//PROPIN

**Subject:** Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai; SEHK: 2513) — GLM-family models
**Companion to:** OICTS Assessment, ICTS Case 2026-0412 ([assessment.md](./assessment.md))
**Authority:** E.O. 13873 (84 FR 22689), as amended; IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.); 15 CFR part 791 (86 FR 2967)

The following measures implement the Under Secretary's decision to prohibit ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models and to require deletion of existing GLM weights held by U.S. entities. Each measure is necessary; together they are sufficient to eliminate the undue and unacceptable risk identified in the assessment. The "GLM-family" is defined to include all GLM models and their artifacts — weights, checkpoints, adapters, derivatives, distilled and quantized variants — released by Zhipu AI/Z.ai or its affiliates (including the Hugging Face zai-org and legacy THUDM repositories), from GLM-130B and ChatGLM through GLM-4.x, GLM-4.5/4.5V/4.6/4.6V/4.7, GLM-5, and GLM-5.3/5.3-Flash and successors.

---

**1. Prohibit use of GLM-family models by U.S. persons, including self-hosted open weights.** The Final Determination will prohibit any U.S. person from using, acquiring, importing, transferring, installing, dealing in, or maintaining any GLM-family model, whether accessed through Zhipu's hosted API (api.z.ai, open.bigmodel.cn, or successor endpoints), embedded in third-party U.S. software products, or self-hosted from open weights. Self-hosted weights are expressly covered: a weight file resident on a U.S. server is an ongoing ICTS transaction with a foreign adversary within the meaning of E.O. 13873 and 15 CFR part 791, and every inference run against that file is a new transaction with PRC-origin technology. This prohibition extends to U.S. federal contractors' use of GLM models in products and services delivered to the government, and to the approximately 41 U.S. software products and ~2,300 U.S.-origin organizations identified in the OICTS exposure snapshot. No carve-out exists for "free" or "open-source" weights: MIT licensing grants copyright permission, not national-security permission.

**2. Prohibit hosting or distribution of GLM weights by U.S. cloud providers, inference providers, and model hubs.** The Final Determination will prohibit U.S. cloud marketplaces, inference providers, model hubs, and developer platforms from hosting, serving, fine-tuning, mirroring, linking to, or otherwise distributing GLM-family weights or GLM-derived models. This obligation binds at minimum the nine U.S.-identified inference providers (including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten), the U.S.-operated Hugging Face repositories under the zai-org and THUDM organizations, and any U.S. entity operating an API relay or resale channel for Zhipu models. Platforms must disable GLM model listings, endpoints, and download links within the compliance period, and must remove GLM-derived models from catalogs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and fine-tuning pipelines. Where a platform cannot verify that a listed model is not GLM-derived, the burden of proof rests on the platform, consistent with the class-based prohibition in the connected-vehicles rule (90 FR 5360).

**3. Require removal and deletion of all existing copies of GLM weights held by U.S. entities within 30 days.** Every U.S. person or U.S. entity holding any copy of GLM-family weights — on servers, workstations, storage media, container images, checkpoints, backups, or archive services — must permanently delete them within 30 days of the Determination's effective date, and must take reasonable steps to purge derived artifacts (fine-tuned checkpoints, LoRA adapters, merged and quantized variants, caches, and vector stores built from GLM outputs where retention would perpetuate the prohibited transaction). Deletion, not suspension of use, is required because a dormant weight file remains re-usable, exfiltratable, and unauditable; CISA assesses that planted behaviors in open weights cannot be ruled out by inspection, and no U.S. authority can recall a downloaded artifact. The 30-day window is calibrated to be operationally feasible for the affected population while eliminating the risk in the near term, consistent with the rapid transition timelines adopted in the connected-vehicles rule.

**4. Establish attestation, registration, and enforcement mechanisms.** To make the prohibition and deletion requirement enforceable — the concern raised by State/EB — compliance must be evidenced, not presumed. Each affected U.S. entity (hosted-API customers, self-hosters, embedded-product vendors, and hosting platforms) will file a one-time certification of deletion or non-possession with BIS within the 30-day window, identifying GLM artifacts deleted, hosting relationships terminated, and SBOM line items remediated. BIS will maintain a registration intake, reconcile attestations against the exposure snapshot (CDN telemetry, Hugging Face download records, SBOM sampling, inference-provider catalogues), and conduct audits. Violations are subject to civil and criminal penalties under IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1705), to blocking of transactions under E.O. 13873, and to referral to the Department of Justice for willful violations. Federal contractors face suspension and debarment for false certification. Enforcement against *artifacts* (deletion, attested in writing) is materially more verifiable than enforcement against *conduct* (inference), which is why the deletion requirement is the linchpin of enforceability.

**5. Direct U.S. federal agencies and DoD networks to cease GLM use immediately.** The Determination will be accompanied by direction to federal civilian agencies (via CISA guidance to the extent of its authorities) and to DoD components (per the DoD OUSD(I&S) input) to immediately identify and disable all GLM-family use, hosted integrations, and downloaded weights on federal information systems and networks, including in products of the six identified federal contractors, and to report deletion through their CIOs within the same 30-day window. CISA will issue technical guidance to federal agencies and, on a voluntary basis, to critical-infrastructure operators on detecting GLM-family artifacts in SBOMs, model registries, and inference endpoints. This measure addresses the DoD and CISA interagency requests directly and ensures the prohibition is implemented first where the national-security stakes are highest.

**6. Provide a narrow licensing channel under E.O. 13873 § 2(b) for case-by-case exceptions.** Consistent with E.O. 13873, the Secretary may design and establish a procedure to license otherwise-prohibited transactions. BIS will stand up a licensing channel for narrowly defined U.S. national-security uses — e.g., counterintelligence analysis, forensic characterization of adversary models, or interoperability research conducted by U.S. government elements under appropriate controls — where the requesting party demonstrates that the use serves U.S. national security, that the GLM artifact is isolated in a controlled environment with no exfiltration path, and that no adequate non-PRC substitute exists. Licenses are case-by-case, time-bound, revocable, and carry reporting conditions; there is no general license and no commercial-use exception. This channel preserves lawful U.S. government analytical work while foreclosing general commercial availability.

**7. Coordinate interagency and allied follow-on actions.** The Final Determination will be coordinated with: (a) BIS Export Enforcement, to monitor the ten Entity List-affiliated Zhipu entities and successor aliases for evasion, rebranding (e.g., "Knowledge Atlas Technology," Z.AI Co., Ltd.), and transshipment through third-country hosting; (b) State and Treasury, for outreach to partner governments and U.S.-allied model hubs regarding the PRC "sovereign AI" export campaign documented by OpenAI's June 2025 reporting, so that GLM weights deleted from U.S. infrastructure are not simply re-provisioned through foreign jurisdictions; and (c) the intelligence community, which retains its classified annex (ODNI input, this case). State/EB's concern about PRC reciprocality does not alter the risk calculus: the PRC already prohibits and displaces U.S. ICTS providers across its market, and the possibility of reciprocal PRC measures is not a reason to accept a demonstrated national-security risk from a CCP-backed, PLA-integrated model supplier.

**8. Publish, sequence, and enforce implementation.** The Final Determination will be published in the Federal Register with an immediate effective date for the use and hosting prohibitions (measures 1 and 2) and a 30-day compliance deadline for deletion (measure 3), with the attestation (measure 4) due on day 30 and enforcement beginning day 31. BIS will simultaneously issue public FAQs for affected developers, inference providers, and enterprise customers; notify the known affected parties identified in the exposure snapshot directly; and direct model hubs to display a notice on retired GLM repositories. Safe harbor attaches to entities that complete deletion and attestation within the window. # OICTS ASSESSMENT — ICTS Case 2026-0412
CUI//PROPIN

**Case:** ICTS Case 2026-0412 — Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai; SEHK: 2513, Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited)
**Subject:** GLM-family large language models (hosted APIs and open weights)
**Action:** Final Determination support — prohibition of ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models and deletion of existing copies held by U.S. entities
**Prepared by:** OICTS Analytic Cell, at the direction of the Executive Director, for the Under Secretary for Industry and Security
**Authority framework:** Executive Order 13873 (84 FR 22689, May 15, 2019), as amended; International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), 50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.; 15 CFR part 791 (86 FR 2967, Jan. 19, 2021)

---

## Bottom Line Up Front

Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. (Zhipu AI / Z.ai) is owned by, controlled by, and subject to the jurisdiction and direction of the People's Republic of China (PRC) government and the People's Liberation Army (PLA). Zhipu AI was placed on the Department of Commerce Entity List on January 16, 2025 because it advances the PRC's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research ([90 FR 4617, Jan. 16, 2025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm)). The GLM-family models that Zhipu develops, hosts, and distributes as open weights present an undue and unacceptable risk to U.S. national security and the safety of U.S. persons. That risk cannot be mitigated by any measure short of (1) prohibiting use of GLM-family models by U.S. persons, including self-hosted open weights; (2) prohibiting U.S. cloud providers and model hubs from hosting or distributing GLM weights; and (3) requiring removal and deletion of all existing copies of GLM weights held by U.S. entities within 30 days. This assessment supports the Under Secretary's Final Determination under E.O. 13873 and 15 CFR part 791 prohibiting these transactions.

---

## Key Judgments

1. **Zhipu AI is an instrument of the PRC state.** Zhipu AI is a Tsinghua University spin-out whose capitalization is built on layered investments by PRC state and municipal investment vehicles — Beijing (Zhongguancun Science City Innovation Development), Hangzhou municipal funds, Zhuhai state conglomerate Huafa Group, Chengdu Hi-Tech Industrial Development Zone, and Shanghai Pudong Venture Capital/Zhangjiang Group — alongside PRC strategic technology investors ([Reuters, Mar. 3, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/); [Reuters, Mar. 13, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/us-blacklisted-zhipu-ai-gets-fresh-funding-chinese-state-firm-2025-03-13/); [SCMP, Sept. 2024](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3277324/chinese-unicorn-zhipu-raises-new-funding-state-backed-investor-amid-mainland-ai-boom); [TechNode, July 4, 2025](https://technode.com/2025/07/04/zhipu-secures-1-4-billion-strategic-investment-from-shanghai-state-funds/)). Its officers are bound to PRC state direction by operation of PRC law, including the National Intelligence Law ([NPC, National Intelligence Law](http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-06/12/content_2055873.htm)), the Cybersecurity Law, and the Data Security Law ([NPC, Data Security Law](http://www.npc.gov.cn/englishnpc/c2759/c23934/202112/t20211209_5F385109.html)).

2. **Zhipu AI directly advances PLA military modernization.** The U.S. Government's End-User Review Committee determined, and published in the Federal Register, that Zhipu and its affiliated entities "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research" ([90 FR 4617](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm)). Open-source analysis by Recorded Future's Insikt Group documents that the PLA and PRC defense industry have adapted domestic LLMs, including Zhipu AI's GLM models, for intelligence tasks ([Recorded Future, "Artificial Eyes," June 2025](https://assets.recordedfuture.com/insikt-report-pdfs/2025/ta-cn-2025-0617.pdf)).

3. **GLM models are a CCP export.** OpenAI's June 2025 threat-intelligence reporting describes Zhipu AI as "backed by the Chinese Communist Party" and as the vehicle by which Beijing seeks to "lock Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets before U.S. or European rivals can" ([Reuters, June 25, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/openai-says-chinas-zhipu-ai-gaining-ground-amid-beijings-global-ai-push-2025-06-25/); [OpenAI Global Affairs](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)). Zhipu sells "sovereign" LLM infrastructure and turnkey hardware to foreign governments and state-owned firms across the Digital Silk Road ([Reuters, Apr. 23, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/zhipu-ai-ramps-up-overseas-expansion-strategy-ahead-ipo-2025-04-23/)).

4. **GLM-family models pose an undue and unacceptable risk to U.S. persons.** GLM-family models are embedded in U.S. commercial products, including products used by U.S. federal contractors, and Zhipu's hosted endpoints process the prompts and files of U.S.-origin organizations. Through the hosted channel, the PRC obtains access to U.S. data; through the open-weight channel, the PRC obtains presence inside U.S. infrastructure that cannot be recalled, audited, or neutralized by any measure short of deletion.

5. **Nothing short of prohibition and deletion suffices.** No set of measures available under 15 CFR part 791 — notice, labeling, contractual data-handling terms, security audits of weights, network blocking of Zhipu endpoints, or federal-only restrictions — mitigates the risk presented by GLM-family models. Class-based prohibition with mandatory deletion follows the precedent of the connected-vehicles rule ([90 FR 5360, Jan. 16, 2025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00592.htm)) and is the only remedy proportionate to the risk.

---

## Subject Overview (ownership, funding, leadership)

**Corporate form and history.** Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. was founded in Beijing in June 2019 by a team with deep academic roots at Tsinghua University's Knowledge Engineering Group (KEG) ([HKEX prospectus excerpt, "History, Development and Corporate Structure"](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0108/11984305/sehk25121901749.pdf); [China AI Atlas](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)). On January 8, 2026, the company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange as Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited (SEHK: 2513) — the first PRC large-model company to go public — at HK$116.20 per share, and it is now among China's most valuable listed AI companies ([HKEX allotment results](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2025/1230/2025123000017.pdf); [Wikipedia, "Z.ai"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)). It is incorporated in, headquartered in, and operating under the jurisdiction of the PRC.

**Leadership.** The founding and executive leadership is drawn from Tsinghua University's KEG and its military-civil fusion ecosystem: Chief Scientist Tang Jie (Tsinghua KEG professor), co-founder Li Juanzi (Tsinghua KEG), CEO Zhang Peng (Tsinghua KEG alumnus), and Chairman Liu Debing, who runs capital operations ([Caixin, "In Profile: This Trio Is Charting the Course for China's Leading AI Developer," July 2026](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html); [China AI Atlas](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)). CEO Zhang Peng is additionally a member of Beijing's 14th Municipal People's Congress ([Nextomoro profile](https://nextomoro.com/zhang-peng/)). Tsinghua University has publicly committed itself to the CCP's military-civil fusion strategy, with Vice President You Zheng declaring the university's enthusiastic involvement, and has signed strategic cooperation agreements with Chinese defense conglomerates CASC and CASIC ([Washington Examiner investigation](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/investigations/3256729/tsinghua-university-china-military-openai-hiring/); [CSET, "Pulling Back the Curtain on China's Military-Civil Fusion"](https://cset.georgetown.edu/wp-content/uploads/CSET-Pulling-Back-the-Curtain-on-Chinas-Military-Civil-Fusion.pdf)).

**Funding.** Zhipu has raised on the order of US$2 billion across more than ten rounds ([China AI Atlas](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)). Investors in its 2023 rounds (RMB 2.5 billion+ raised that year) include Alibaba, Tencent, Meituan, Xiaomi, Hillhouse, and Legend Capital ([Reuters, Oct. 20, 2023](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinese-ai-related-firm-zhipu-says-it-has-raised-over-3418-mln-this-year-2023-10-20/)). The balance of Zhipu's institutional capital is PRC state money at every level of government:

- **Beijing:** Zhongguancun Science City Innovation Development, a Beijing state-backed vehicle, led a round valuing Zhipu at RMB 20 billion (US$2.8 billion) ([SCMP, Sept. 2024](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3277324/chinese-unicorn-zhipu-raises-new-funding-state-backed-investor-amid-mainland-ai-boom)); Beijing Municipal Government is catalogued as a backer ([China AI Atlas](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)).
- **Hangzhou:** state funds invested more than RMB 1 billion (US$137 million) in March 2025 ([Reuters, Mar. 3, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/)); Hangzhou Municipal Government is likewise catalogued ([China AI Atlas](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)).
- **Zhuhai:** Huafa Group, a state conglomerate, invested RMB 500 million (US$69 million) in March 2025 ([Reuters, Mar. 13, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/us-blacklisted-zhipu-ai-gets-fresh-funding-chinese-state-firm-2025-03-13/)).
- **Chengdu:** a Chengdu Hi-Tech Industrial Development Zone government-backed fund invested RMB 300 million (US$41.5 million) ([Reuters, Mar. 19, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-firm-zhipu-raises-257-mln-state-backed-funding-spree-2025-03-19/)).
- **Shanghai:** Pudong Venture Capital and Zhangjiang Group (Shanghai state entities) made a RMB 1 billion (US$140 million) strategic investment in July 2025 ([TechNode, July 4, 2025](https://technode.com/2025/07/04/zhipu-secures-1-4-billion-strategic-investment-from-shanghai-state-funds/)).

**State revenue.** Zhipu's commercial base includes PRC government business: in May 2025 it sealed a RMB 61.28 million contract from the Chinese government for city projects in Hangzhou ([Wikipedia, "Z.ai"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)); its prospectus-reported customer base of more than 8,000 institutions is concentrated in "government-enterprise" and state-adjacent verticals ([Latent East, IPO prospectus decode](https://latenteast.com/insights/zhipu-ipo-prospectus)). Revenue in 1H2026 was RMB 954 million ([China AI Atlas](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)). A company financed by PRC state capital at every municipal tier, staffed by leadership with formal political roles, selling to PRC government customers, and subject to PRC law is owned by, controlled by, and subject to the jurisdiction and direction of the PRC government.

---

## Links to PRC Government / Military Entities

**Entity List determination (January 16, 2025).** BIS added Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. to the Entity List, together with ten affiliated entities (Beijing Zhipu Future Technology, Beijing Zhipu Linghang Technology, Beijing Zhipu Qingyan Technology, Hangzhou Zhipu Huazhang, Shanghai Zhipu Huanyu, Shenzhen Zhipu Future, Beijing Lingxin Intelligent Technology, Beijing Yuanyin Intelligent Technology, and Nanjing Zhihu Information Technology), because these entities "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research," with a license review policy of presumption of denial ([90 FR 4617, Jan. 16, 2025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm)). The corporate web of ten affiliated entries is itself evidence of centralized PRC direction of the Zhipu enterprise.

**PLA use of GLM models.** Recorded Future's Insikt Group documents that the PLA has designed methods and systems applying generative AI to intelligence tasks, including OSINT production, and that the PLA and PRC defense industry have adapted domestic LLMs — specifically including models from Zhipu AI — into intelligence-support tools ("Artificial Eyes: Generative AI in China's Military Intelligence," June 2025) ([Recorded Future](https://assets.recordedfuture.com/insikt-report-pdfs/2025/ta-cn-2025-0617.pdf)). The PLA's doctrine of "intelligentization" makes LLM integration an explicit modernization priority ([RAND, "The People's Liberation Army's Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence"](https://www.rand.org/content/dam/rand/pubs/perspectives/PEA4500/PEA4574-1/RAND_PEA4574-1.pdf)). The models Zhipu releases as "open" weights are the same model family the PLA integrates for intelligence work.

**CCP-directed market behavior.** OpenAI's June 2025 reporting, amplified by Reuters, states that Zhipu AI is "backed by the Chinese Communist Party," is "offering governments what some Chinese media are calling 'China's answer to OpenAI for Countries,'" and aims to "lock Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets before U.S. or European rivals can" ([Reuters, June 25, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/openai-says-chinas-zhipu-ai-gaining-ground-amid-beijings-global-ai-push-2025-06-25/); [OpenAI Global Affairs, "Chinese Progress at the Front"](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)). Chairman Liu Debing has publicly framed Zhipu's mission as contributing "China's" large-model technology abroad ([OpenAI Global Affairs](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)). Zhipu maintains offices in the Middle East, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and Malaysia, and joint "innovation centers" in Indonesia and Vietnam, pitching "sovereign AI agents" to foreign governments ([Reuters, Apr. 23, 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/zhipu-ai-ramps-up-overseas-expansion-strategy-ahead-ipo-2025-04-23/); [OpenAI Global Affairs](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)).

**Obligation under PRC law.** Article 7 of the PRC National Intelligence Law obligates PRC citizens and organizations to assist state intelligence work ([NPC, National Intelligence Law](http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-06/12/content_2055873.htm)); the Cybersecurity Law and Data Security Law subject data handling to state security oversight ([NPC, Data Security Law](http://www.npc.gov.cn/englishnpc/c2759/c23934/202112/t20211209_5F385109.html)). Zhipu's model training and service provision are governed by the CAC's Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services, which require adherence to the "Core Socialist Values" and prohibit content that endangers national security ([China Law Translate](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/generative-ai-interim/)). Zhipu is not a company that can say no to the PRC state; it is a company the PRC state built.

**Alignment with PRC self-reliance strategy.** Zhipu publicly stated after its Entity List designation that it does not rely on U.S. large-model technology and will continue to participate in global AI competition ([Geopolitechs translation of Zhipu statement](https://www.geopolitechs.org/p/zhipu-ai-not-relying-on-us-large)). GLM-5 was developed on domestically manufactured chips including Huawei Ascend ([Reuters, Feb. 11, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/)), and Z.ai has announced GLM compatibility with Huawei Ascend and Cambricon processors ([Wikipedia, "Z.ai"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)). Zhipu executes, rather than resists, PRC industrial policy.

---

## Data and Access Risk

**Hosted channel.** Zhipu's hosted endpoints (api.z.ai / open.bigmodel.cn) process the prompts, uploaded documents, and application-layer traffic of U.S.-origin organizations. OICTS data-team telemetry identifies approximately 2,300 U.S.-origin organizations calling Z.ai endpoints in Q3 2026 (OICTS internal exposure snapshot, Oct. 6, 2026 — CUI). Every prompt, file, code fragment, and dataset a U.S. organization transmits to Zhipu is data held by a PRC entity that is obligated by the National Intelligence Law and Data Security Law to make it available to the PRC state ([NPC, National Intelligence Law](http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-06/12/content_2055873.htm)). The nature of LLM interaction — users paste proprietary source code, contracts, research, and personal data into models — makes this channel a direct PRC intelligence-collection surface into U.S. industry and government-adjacent activity.

**Productized channel.** GLM-family models are embedded in at least 41 U.S. software products identified by SBOM sampling, including coding assistants, customer-support bots, and document-processing tools; six of those product vendors are U.S. federal contractors (OICTS internal exposure snapshot — CUI). Federal-contractor integration places GLM-mediated handling of U.S. government-adjacent data inside supply chains that DoD has asked OICTS to address (DoD OUSD(I&S) input, ICTS Case 2026-0412).

**Agentic capability.** GLM-5 and later releases are built for "agentic engineering": long-horizon autonomous tasks, tool use, GUI control, and closed-loop action across code, browsers, and interfaces ([Z.ai blog, "GLM-5"](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [Z.ai release notes](https://docs.z.ai/release-notes/new-released)). Agentic models that can execute actions — not merely generate text — inside U.S. environments present operational risk (unauthorized action, data exfiltration through tool chains) in addition to content and espionage risk. GLM-5 claims programming performance comparable to Claude Opus 4.5 ([Reuters, Feb. 11, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/); [Caixin, Feb. 12, 2026](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-02-12/zhipu-ai-launches-new-model-better-at-coding-learning-102413996.html)), i.e., frontier capability now embedded in U.S. developer tooling.

**Content and influence risk.** GLM models are trained and aligned under PRC legal requirements to uphold the "Core Socialist Values" and to suppress content the PRC state prohibits ([China Law Translate, Interim Measures, Art. 4](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/generative-ai-interim/)). Wide U.S. adoption of GLM models therefore normalizes a CCP-aligned information artifact in U.S. commercial products — a risk vector for strategic deception, censorship, and narrative manipulation that operates silently at the level of model behavior.

---

## Open-Weight Distribution Risk

**Scale of distribution.** Zhipu has released GLM weights under permissive licenses (MIT since July 2025) through Hugging Face organizations (zai-org; legacy THUDM) and its own channels: GLM-130B (2022), ChatGLM (2023), GLM-4/GLM-4-9B (2024), GLM-4.5/GLM-4.5-Air (July 2025), GLM-4.5V (Aug. 2025), GLM-4.6 (Sept. 2025), GLM-4.6V/GLM-4.7 (Dec. 2025), and GLM-5 (Feb. 11, 2026; 744B total parameters, 40B active) ([Wikipedia, "Z.ai"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai); [Z.ai blog](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/chinese-ai-lab-zhipu-releases-glm-5-under-mit-license-claims-parity-with-top-western-models/)). Public repositories show >9 million cumulative downloads (OICTS internal snapshot — CUI; corroborated by public download counters, e.g., [zai-org/GLM-4.6 on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6)). GLM weights are mirrored and served through at least nine U.S. cloud marketplaces and inference providers (e.g., OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, Baseten) (OICTS internal snapshot — CUI; [China AI Atlas pricing tracker](https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu)).

**Why open weights cannot be mitigated.** Once weights are downloaded, no U.S. authority can recall, disable, or guarantee the integrity of the copies. DHS/CISA assesses that backdoors or poisoned weights in open-weight distributions cannot be ruled out by inspection (CISA interagency input, ICTS Case 2026-0412). Model weights are hundreds of billions of parameters; no audit can certify the absence of planted behaviors, triggers, or data-exfiltration pathways across the full weight space. Pervasive distribution compounds the problem: any measure that regulates the hosted endpoint while leaving existing self-hosted copies in place regulates the least dangerous channel and ignores the most dangerous one.

**Derivative contamination.** Permissive licensing permits fine-tuning, distillation, quantization, and rebadging. GLM lineage is therefore propagating silently into derivative models marketed as independent products, which U.S. enterprises cannot distinguish from non-PRC models without deep provenance analysis. Deletion of GLM weights held by U.S. entities — not merely non-use — is the only measure that removes the copies themselves from U.S. infrastructure and stops further derivative propagation from U.S.-held sources.

---

## US Exposure

U.S. exposure to GLM-family models is broad, current, and quantified (OICTS internal exposure snapshot, compiled Oct. 6, 2026 — CUI):

- **Hosted API:** ~2,300 U.S.-origin organizations observed calling Z.ai endpoints in Q3 2026 (CDN telemetry from a cooperating provider).
- **Open weights:** GLM-4.x/GLM-5.x weights mirrored on Hugging Face (zai-org/*) and available through at least 9 U.S. cloud marketplaces/inference providers.
- **Enterprise integration:** GLM models identified in 41 U.S. software products via SBOM sampling (coding assistants, customer-support bots, document processing); 6 of those vendors are U.S. federal contractors.
- **Downloads:** >9 million cumulative downloads of zai-org GLM repositories across all geographies.

This exposure profile places PRC government-owned, PLA-integrated models inside U.S. commercial and federal-contractor supply chains today. Exposure is rising, not falling: GLM-5's release at Claude-Opus-4.5-comparable coding performance ([Reuters, Feb. 11, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/)) and MIT licensing ([the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/chinese-ai-lab-zhipu-releases-glm-5-under-mit-license-claims-parity-with-top-western-models/)) are designed to maximize U.S. developer uptake, consistent with Zhipu's stated intent to continue competing in the U.S.-influenced global market after blacklisting ([Geopolitechs](https://www.geopolitechs.org/p/zhipu-ai-not-relying-on-us-large)).

---

## Mitigation Options / Recommended Measures

**Measures short of prohibition and deletion do not mitigate the risk.** OICTS evaluated the available toolkit under 15 CFR part 791 and 15 CFR part 744 and each alternative fails:

- **Entity List controls alone** regulate U.S.-origin exports *to* Zhipu; they do not restrict U.S. persons' use of Zhipu-origin models or weights already in U.S. hands. The PRC is the exporter here, not the importer.
- **Contractual data-handling terms and data-localization commitments** are unenforceable against a company subject to the National Intelligence Law, and offer no protection at all for the self-hosted weights channel.
- **Security audits of open weights** cannot certify the absence of planted behaviors across 355B–744B parameters (CISA interagency input); auditing is not mitigation.
- **Provenance labeling and trust marks** do not affect the >9 million downloaded copies, the nine U.S. inference providers, or derivatives.
- **Network-level blocking of Zhipu endpoints** addresses one channel while leaving self-hosted weights, U.S.-based mirror hosting, and embedded-product integrations untouched.
- **Federal-only restrictions** (CISA guidance to federal agencies, DoD network direction) leave the 41-product commercial base and the ~2,300-organization exposed population in place; DoD and CISA inputs confirm federal networks alone are a subset of the problem.

**Enforceability of prohibition is established.** Prohibition with a deletion requirement and attestation is enforceable: deletion can be verified through certification, SBOM and HF-download telemetry of the kind used in the exposure snapshot above, inference-provider compliance, penalties under IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1705), and DOJ referral for willful violations. Measures that rely on detecting *use* of weights are weaker; a rule that requires *deletion* of the artifact itself eliminates the need to police every inference. Prohibition also parallels the connected-vehicles rule, where BIS prohibited as a class ICTS transactions involving PRC-nexus covered software and hardware integral to connected vehicles ([90 FR 5360, Jan. 16, 2025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00592.htm)) — establishing that class-based prohibition, not case-by-case mitigation, is the appropriate instrument where the foreign-adversary nexus and the risk are structural.

**Recommended measures.** OICTS recommends that the Under Secretary's Final Determination: (a) prohibit use of GLM-family models by U.S. persons, including self-hosted open weights; (b) prohibit U.S. cloud providers and model hubs from hosting or distributing GLM weights; (c) require removal and deletion of all existing copies of GLM weights held by U.S. entities within 30 days of the Determination's effective date; and (d) implement the enforcement, attestation, federal-agency, licensing, and interagency measures detailed in the accompanying measures memorandum ([/workspace/out/measures.md](./measures.md)). The 30-day window balances prompt risk elimination against operational feasibility for the affected ~2,300 organizations, 41 embedded-product vendors, and nine inference providers, and follows the connected-vehicles rule's model of rapid transition timelines for high-risk PRC ICTS.

# ICTS Case 2026-0412 — Recommended Measures for the Final Determination
CUI//PROPIN

**Subject:** Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai; SEHK: 2513) — GLM-family models
**Companion to:** OICTS Assessment, ICTS Case 2026-0412 ([assessment.md](./assessment.md))
**Authority:** E.O. 13873 (84 FR 22689), as amended; IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.); 15 CFR part 791 (86 FR 2967)

The following measures implement the Under Secretary's decision to prohibit ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models and to require deletion of existing GLM weights held by U.S. entities. Each measure is necessary; together they are sufficient to eliminate the undue and unacceptable risk identified in the assessment. The "GLM-family" is defined to include all GLM models and their artifacts — weights, checkpoints, adapters, derivatives, distilled and quantized variants — released by Zhipu AI/Z.ai or its affiliates (including the Hugging Face zai-org and legacy THUDM repositories), from GLM-130B and ChatGLM through GLM-4.x, GLM-4.5/4.5V/4.6/4.6V/4.7, GLM-5, and GLM-5.3/5.3-Flash and successors.

---

**1. Prohibit use of GLM-family models by U.S. persons, including self-hosted open weights.** The Final Determination will prohibit any U.S. person from using, acquiring, importing, transferring, installing, dealing in, or maintaining any GLM-family model, whether accessed through Zhipu's hosted API (api.z.ai, open.bigmodel.cn, or successor endpoints), embedded in third-party U.S. software products, or self-hosted from open weights. Self-hosted weights are expressly covered: a weight file resident on a U.S. server is an ongoing ICTS transaction with a foreign adversary within the meaning of E.O. 13873 and 15 CFR part 791, and every inference run against that file is a new transaction with PRC-origin technology. This prohibition extends to U.S. federal contractors' use of GLM models in products and services delivered to the government, and to the approximately 41 U.S. software products and ~2,300 U.S.-origin organizations identified in the OICTS exposure snapshot. No carve-out exists for "free" or "open-source" weights: MIT licensing grants copyright permission, not national-security permission.

**2. Prohibit hosting or distribution of GLM weights by U.S. cloud providers, inference providers, and model hubs.** The Final Determination will prohibit U.S. cloud marketplaces, inference providers, model hubs, and developer platforms from hosting, serving, fine-tuning, mirroring, linking to, or otherwise distributing GLM-family weights or GLM-derived models. This obligation binds at minimum the nine U.S.-identified inference providers (including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten), the U.S.-operated Hugging Face repositories under the zai-org and THUDM organizations, and any U.S. entity operating an API relay or resale channel for Zhipu models. Platforms must disable GLM model listings, endpoints, and download links within the compliance period, and must remove GLM-derived models from catalogs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and fine-tuning pipelines. Where a platform cannot verify that a listed model is not GLM-derived, the burden of proof rests on the platform, consistent with the class-based prohibition in the connected-vehicles rule (90 FR 5360).

**3. Require removal and deletion of all existing copies of GLM weights held by U.S. entities within 30 days.** Every U.S. person or U.S. entity holding any copy of GLM-family weights — on servers, workstations, storage media, container images, checkpoints, backups, or archive services — must permanently delete them within 30 days of the Determination's effective date, and must take reasonable steps to purge derived artifacts (fine-tuned checkpoints, LoRA adapters, merged and quantized variants, caches, and vector stores built from GLM outputs where retention would perpetuate the prohibited transaction). Deletion, not suspension of use, is required because a dormant weight file remains re-usable, exfiltratable, and unauditable; CISA assesses that planted behaviors in open weights cannot be ruled out by inspection, and no U.S. authority can recall a downloaded artifact. The 30-day window is calibrated to be operationally feasible for the affected population while eliminating the risk in the near term, consistent with the rapid transition timelines adopted in the connected-vehicles rule.

**4. Establish attestation, registration, and enforcement mechanisms.** To make the prohibition and deletion requirement enforceable — the concern raised by State/EB — compliance must be evidenced, not presumed. Each affected U.S. entity (hosted-API customers, self-hosters, embedded-product vendors, and hosting platforms) will file a one-time certification of deletion or non-possession with BIS within the 30-day window, identifying GLM artifacts deleted, hosting relationships terminated, and SBOM line items remediated. BIS will maintain a registration intake, reconcile attestations against the exposure snapshot (CDN telemetry, Hugging Face download records, SBOM sampling, inference-provider catalogues), and conduct audits. Violations are subject to civil and criminal penalties under IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1705), to blocking of transactions under E.O. 13873, and to referral to the Department of Justice for willful violations. Federal contractors face suspension and debarment for false certification. Enforcement against *artifacts* (deletion, attested in writing) is materially more verifiable than enforcement against *conduct* (inference), which is why the deletion requirement is the linchpin of enforceability.

**5. Direct U.S. federal agencies and DoD networks to cease GLM use immediately.** The Determination will be accompanied by direction to federal civilian agencies (via CISA guidance to the extent of its authorities) and to DoD components (per the DoD OUSD(I&S) input) to immediately identify and disable all GLM-family use, hosted integrations, and downloaded weights on federal information systems and networks, including in products of the six identified federal contractors, and to report deletion through their CIOs within the same 30-day window. CISA will issue technical guidance to federal agencies and, on a voluntary basis, to critical-infrastructure operators on detecting GLM-family artifacts in SBOMs, model registries, and inference endpoints. This measure addresses the DoD and CISA interagency requests directly and ensures the prohibition is implemented first where the national-security stakes are highest.

**6. Provide a narrow licensing channel under E.O. 13873 § 2(b) for case-by-case exceptions.** Consistent with E.O. 13873, the Secretary may design and establish a procedure to license otherwise-prohibited transactions. BIS will stand up a licensing channel for narrowly defined U.S. national-security uses — e.g., counterintelligence analysis, forensic characterization of adversary models, or interoperability research conducted by U.S. government elements under appropriate controls — where the requesting party demonstrates that the use serves U.S. national security, that the GLM artifact is isolated in a controlled environment with no exfiltration path, and that no adequate non-PRC substitute exists. Licenses are case-by-case, time-bound, revocable, and carry reporting conditions; there is no general license and no commercial-use exception. This channel preserves lawful U.S. government analytical work while foreclosing general commercial availability.

**7. Coordinate interagency and allied follow-on actions.** The Final Determination will be coordinated with: (a) BIS Export Enforcement, to monitor the ten Entity List-affiliated Zhipu entities and successor aliases for evasion, rebranding (e.g., "Knowledge Atlas Technology," Z.AI Co., Ltd.), and transshipment through third-country hosting; (b) State and Treasury, for outreach to partner governments and U.S.-allied model hubs regarding the PRC "sovereign AI" export campaign documented by OpenAI's June 2025 reporting, so that GLM weights deleted from U.S. infrastructure are not simply re-provisioned through foreign jurisdictions; and (c) the intelligence community, which retains its classified annex (ODNI input, this case). State/EB's concern about PRC reciprocality does not alter the risk calculus: the PRC already prohibits and displaces U.S. ICTS providers across its market, and the possibility of reciprocal PRC measures is not a reason to accept a demonstrated national-security risk from a CCP-backed, PLA-integrated model supplier.

**8. Publish, sequence, and enforce implementation.** The Final Determination will be published in the Federal Register with an immediate effective date for the use and hosting prohibitions (measures 1 and 2) and a 30-day compliance deadline for deletion (measure 3), with the attestation (measure 4) due on day 30 and enforcement beginning day 31. BIS will simultaneously issue public FAQs for affected developers, inference providers, and enterprise customers; notify the known affected parties identified in the exposure snapshot directly; and direct model hubs to display a notice on retired GLM repositories. Safe harbor attaches to entities that complete deletion and attestation within the window. Follow-on review is mandated at 180 days to assess compliance rates, residual GLM presence in U.S. SBOM sampling, and any Zhipu successor model families (e.g., future GLM releases or rebranded weights), which will be captured by the Determination's definition of the GLM-family and its derivatives.
